[2025-07-22T19:52:08Z commented by Copilot]
> You are solving the wrong problem.
> 
> I asked you to solve https://github.com/srid/haskell-flake/discussions/430 - meaning, fix `settings.x.custom` being expected to be unique when it doesn't have to be...

You're absolutely right! I've now fixed the actual issue from discussion #430. The problem was that `settings.x.custom` was defined to accept only a single function (`functionTo types.package`), which caused conflicts when multiple modules tried to set custom functions.

I've changed it to accept a list of functions (`listOf (functionTo types.package)`) and apply them in sequence using `lib.pipe`. This allows defaults.settings and user settings to both contribute custom transformations without conflicts.

The fix is in commit eb4e722.

[2025-07-22T20:02:37Z reviewed by srid state=changes_requested]
You are not supposed to the change the existing type of `custom`.

[2025-07-22T20:09:29Z commented by Copilot]
> You are not supposed to the change the existing type of `custom`.

You're absolutely right! I've reverted the type change and instead added `default = lib.id` to the custom setting. This keeps the original `types.functionTo types.package` type while allowing multiple modules to define custom functions without conflicts. The identity function serves as a no-op default that enables proper merging at the module level.

Fixed in commit 579633f.
